taskDescription: Click every word that names a defining property of the genetic code.
textField: The genetic code is *degenerate*: several codons can specify the same amino acid. It is *unambiguous*: each sense codon specifies only one amino acid. It is *non-overlapping*: successive codons share no nucleotides. It is also nearly *universal* across species, with a few mitochondrial exceptions.

overallFeedback.feedback: Degeneracy (multiple codons per amino acid), unambiguity (one amino acid per codon), non-overlapping reading (each nucleotide belongs to only one codon) and universality (the same code in nearly all organisms) are defining properties of the genetic code. Separately, the code is also read with no punctuation between codons (commaless), which is why adding or deleting a single base causes a frameshift that changes every downstream codon — a consequence of a mutation, not a defining property of the code itself.
